correctness.rationale: Coordinate complementing even sites is an orthogonal isometry to a path stable-set polytope. Dynamic programming yields the exact two-sign Gaussian support recursion. Past Gaussian sign resets give unique stationary processes, geometric coupling, and |a_n E W_n-2cn|≤4/√(2π). A -,+ sign pattern regenerates both coordinates; finite-moment iid cycles produce a joint renewal CLT for summed rewards and Gaussian-square sums. Gaussian integration by parts and positive homogeneity give the exact covariance Cov(H_n,Q_n)=E H_n. The spherical delta expansion leads to σ²=τ²-2c² with exact cycle formula, and an exact radial-variance identity proves variance convergence. Two-step cycle rewards vary continuously, proving strict positivity. Finite checker independently tested n≤10 support, isometry, numeric fixed point, radial centering, and covariance identity; no experimental step substitutes for proof.

The closest probabilistic predecessors either concern first-order independent-set means or renewal fluctuations of independently edge-weighted maximal paths, which do not imply coupled signed Gaussian stable-set widths normalized by the same Euclidean radius. value.rationale: Zigzag order and chain polytopes form a natural high-dimensional full-dimensional family with exponentially many vertices. Their random Euclidean projection lengths have a nondegenerate Gaussian fluctuation law with an explicit geometric radial-variance correction, not a classical cube/simplex or arbitrary numerical invariant. The exact renewal representation and finite-size mean error yield a usable distributional model for these polytopes. The result is structural rather than a routine application: it needs two-sign coupled recursion and simultaneous Gaussian-radius fluctuations.
